Client.title: Client
Client.description: Represents a client using the MT5 platform and their license status.

email.description: The email address of the client.

accountNumber.description: The client's account number on the MT5 platform.

brokerServer.description: The broker server the client is connected to.

balanceGross.description: The gross balance of the client's MT5 account.

balanceNet.description: The net balance of the client's MT5 account.

openTradesCount.description: The number of open trades in the client's MT5 account.

openTradesProfit.description: The total profit from open trades in the client's MT5 account.

totalInBRL.description: The total balance in Brazilian Real (BRL).

status.description: The authorization status of the client's license (Liberado/Bloqueado).

lastUpdate.description: The timestamp of the last data update for the client.

CopyMaster.title: Copy Master

CopyOrder.title: Copy Order
CopyOrder.description: Represents a trade order from a master account.

ticket_master.description: The unique ticket ID from the master's MT5.

status.description: The current status of the order.

CopyLicense.title: Copy License
CopyLicense.description: Represents a slave account's license to copy a master.

active.description: Whether the license is active or not.

master_id.description: The ID of the master account to copy.

risk_divider.description: Risk division factor for the slave account.

created_at.description: Timestamp of when the license was created.

last_check.description: Timestamp of the last license check.

firestore.reasoning: The Firestore structure is updated to correctly support the Copy Trade module. The original `/clients` collection remains untouched. Two new root-level collections, `copytrade_masters` and `copytrade_licenses`, are introduced for better isolation, scalability, and query performance. This structure avoids overly nested data, which simplifies API logic and security rules. Using root collections allows for direct queries (e.g., finding all slaves for a master) without needing complex collection group queries, which is critical for the slave limit business rule. This corrected structure is more conventional and robust for Firestore.
